item.title: Violinist Meg Okura Creates a Lush Span of Styles
item.description: Meg Okura creates a unique musical blend, and her new album with the Pan Asian Chamber Jazz Ensemble, Isaiah, is ambitious and lushly accessible.

item.title: Britpop Pioneers Squeeze Bring Out the Fun on ‘Trixies’
item.description: Squeeze were always ambitious, although never at the expense of fun. Trixies is imaginative, impressive, and most importantly, fun.

item.title: Ichi the Killer’s Scar Couture
item.description: Ichi the Killer transcends gangster archetypes, becoming a model of how agony can be elevated to art and self-destruction a powerful form of self-expression.

item.title: Lynn Miles on the Discipline of Emotional Balance
item.description: For Canadian folk singer-songwriter Lynn Miles, yielding to songwriting is not passivity. It is discipline. Attention. Trust.

item.title: Al Stewart’s “Time Passages” Completes His “Year of the Cat”
item.description: Folk-pop-rock singer Al Stewart scored a career-boosting hit with 1976's "Year of the Cat" and continued the momentum with "Time Passages".

item.title: Jackie West Expands the Strengths of Her Brilliant Debut
item.description: Jackie West grows from her immensely satisfying debut album into a follow-up that sees her taking chances while writing beautiful, emotionally striking music.

item.title: William Clark Green Sings About Good Ol’ Texas
item.description: Watterson Hall offers a glimpse into the mythical Texas that many consider their rightful heritage. William Clark Green personifies a good ol' boy without stereotypes.

item.title: Tōth Finds the Clarity of His ‘Voice’ Through Constraint
item.description: Tōth’s And the Voice Said refines his knack for balancing introspection, pop warmth, and unresolved inner tension.

item.title: Mariachi El Bronx Suit Up Again After a Decade Away
item.description: While the idea of hard-core gringo rockers Mariachi El Bronx covering the hyper-emotional Mexican genre might seem like a goof, the musicians dove in and took it seriously.

item.title: Gorillaz at 25 Are a Cultural Force for the Good
item.description: Assuming personal stability is necessary for collective betterment, it's high time that Gorillaz share their newest, loving, bizarre journey with the rest of the world.
